newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian FRN rate fix blamed for uneven MM yields.
newsitem.headline: Belgian FRN rate fix blamed for uneven MM yields.

text.p: A regular four-monthly fixing of floating rate certificates of deposit issued last year by the Belgian central bank was blamed on Wednesday for unevenness in Belgian money market yields.

Compared with three-month T-bills of around 3.26/29 percent and three-month repos at around 3.28/31 percent, one-week and tomorrow/next repos at 3.32/34 and 3.32/38 percent were unusually expensive, dealers said.
Some said, however, the levels had more to do with ongoing uncertainty over economic and monetary union (EMU) and a general lack of liquidity, with many dealers on summer holidays.
One Treasury bill trader said no-one was quite sure what was happening in the money market, noting yields had been high all year and the Belgian franc relatively weak versus the mark.

"It's very hard to understand what's happening. If you look at our spread to Germany, at the long-end, 10-years, it's around seven basis points. In the very short term, it's much higher...around 20 basis points," she said.

The Belgian central bank squeezed liquidity early in 1997 to push up money market yields to support the franc. She said dealers were still very much focused on the bank's money market operations, but they had not much impact.

"Whatever they do it does not seem to affect the level of the franc," she said. The Belgian franc was at 20.6315/25 to the mark at around 0820 GMT, up from overnight levels around 20.6320/35, but off early highs around 20.6305/15.
At the long end the benchmark 10-year OLO yield was flat to higher as the market quietly awaited the results of the U.S. Fed's policy meeting that started Tuesday. No change in rates was expected.
More important was likely to be the June employment report, due unusually on Thursday because U.S. markets are shut on Friday for Independence Day.
